1.
Allowed, subject to the Appellant filing certified copy of the Award within a period of three weeks.
2. The Application stands disposed of.
MAC.APP. 489/2025 & CM APPL. 47964/2025 [Stay]

3. The present Appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [hereinafter referred to as "MV Act"] seeking to challenge the order dated 28.04.2025 passed by the learned Presiding Officer, MACT (South District) Saket, New Delhi [hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Order"].
By the Impugned Order an award in the sum of Rs.2,29,319/- along with 9% interest has been awarded.

4. Learned Counsel for the Appellant submits that he limits his challenge in the present Appeal to a finding of the learned Trial Court which grants pay and recovery rights to the Appellant against Respondent Nos.2 and 3/Driver and owner of the vehicle.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/08/2025 at 23:15:01 5.

Learned Counsel for the Appellant submits that the recovery rights have been granted to the Appellant when the accident took place on 25.10.2022 after the passing of the amendment to the MV Act, whereby the provision for pay and recover was deleted by the amendment.
Thus, it is contended that the Impugned Award, to the extent that it grants the recovery rights, suffers from an infirmity.

An affidavit of service be filed within a week.
7. Subject to the deposit of entire decretal amount inclusive of up-to-date interest within a period of 6 weeks, the operation of the Impugned Award shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing.
In the event, there is any default in depositing the amount, the interim protection granted by this Court shall automatically stand vacated.
8. Concededly, the recovery rights have been granted to the Insurance Company which is contrary to the law as amended by the Motor Vehicle Amendment Act, 2019.

The MV Act is a beneficial legislation and the real object of the MV Act, is to compensate for the loss of earning member of the family or for the injuries suffered by the claimant(s), and the same will be achieved if the compensation can be disbursed without any delay.

8.1 The Supreme Court in the case of Parminder Singh v. Honey Goyal and Others; 2025 SCC OnLine SC 567 has held that MV Act is a beneficial legislation and the object of the MV Act is to compensate for the loss of earning member of the family or for the injuries suffered by the claimant(s), and the same will be achieved if the compensation can be disbursed without any delay.

8.2 Since, the Impugned Award has been kept in abeyance while this issue is decided by the Court, this Court deems it apposite to direct that some amount of compensation once deposited by the Appellant be released to the Respondent/Claimant.

8.3 Upon deposit by the Appellant, 35% of the deposited amount inclusive of up-to-date interest shall be released to the Respondent/claimant in accordance with scheme, as is set out in the Impugned Award.
